messages:
morgan: Quick check — I'm proposing making messages[].role optional to smooth upgrades. Concern: how runtime handles tool/function calls when role is missing. cc @sanjay @elena
sanjay: If role missing we currently default to "user" in the SDK layer. Runtime treats absent role as user for conv routing. But function-call logic expects assistant->function transition. Might be fine but needs test
elena: Question: streaming deltas rely on event_type for func calls. If role absent, do we still emit 'function_call' event? Example snippet:
```json
{"messages":[{"content":"run query","name":"db","type":"tool"}]}
```
zane: That example is missing role+role-based signals. Runtime will still produce a function_call if the model decides, but reassembly assumes message.role present for ordering. We should add reassembly fallback for missing role.
frank: +1 for fallback. Also need to update schema docs and add SDK lint rule to warn when role is omitted.
ci-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/compare/feature/optional-role — tests/notes: streaming reassembly added fallback, SDK lint rule
morgan: thanks. Can we get a quick QA on canary for streaming clients? @sanjay — if we roll this without reassembly fallback, older web clients may misorder toolcall fragments.
sanjay: I'll queue a canary job. Want to coordinate with eng-runtime for telemetry event to detect missing-role fragments. tagging @elena to add eval prompt set
elena: doing it now. I'll add a small eval that simulates partial funccall streaming and checks final reassembly order. ETA 3h :hourglass:
morgan: perfect. if canary looks good we'll ship the lint + docs in same PR or follow-up? prefer same PR to reduce drift
zane: same-PR is cleaner. I'll review tests. :thumbsup:
